question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
8 y^{2}-ye^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y\,,\ y\ne 0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{aligned}8 y^{2}-ye^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=y \\ -ye^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+8 y^{2}-y&=0 \\ -y(e^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8 y+1)&=0 \\ e^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8 y+1&=0 \\ e^{x}(e^{- x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8 y+1)&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8 y e^{x}+e^{x}&=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- 8 e^{x})}_{P(x)}y&=\underbrace{- e^{x}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 8 y e^{x}&=- e^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- 8 e^{x}$ and $Q(x)=- e^{x}.$
